findings.text: non-blocking: moved_gates collects every gate that touches the moved section regardless of status, so a closed gate travels to the successor as well as staying on the closed plan, while the plan requires a closed gate that named only the moved section to stay on the closed plan as evidence and states that the section's open gates travel.

non-blocking: _resolve_successor_section is called without the write's root (here and at :3380), so a write against an explicit checkout root resolves moved_to against the default root, whereas _write_successor_moves at :3091 does pass root; on the documented multi-worktree path a valid move is refused, or the successor half is silently skipped when the payload has no matching section there.

non-blocking: the done_when says the successor carries the moved section's effort as well as its prose, capability and open gate, but the assertions cover only prose, capability, gate and link; nothing reddens if the effort carry at reckon/_store.py:3117 regresses.

non-blocking: SectionRecord.moved_to is a field nothing populates - reckon/_plan_html.py:1597 renders a fixed attribute set with no data-moved-to and no reader parses one - so the field and its validator at :1055 describe a shape the store never writes; the durable record is the data-links entry at reckon/_store.py:2874.
